title: 1113-going-for-goal-grounded-football
universal_lens: Grounded football commentary as a multimodal alignment problem: video frames \( v \) aligned to textual commentaries \( c \) via retrieval \( R(v \to c) \), reordering \( O(f \to c) \), and moment mapping \( M(c \to v) \).
gsi_mapping: Bayesian grounding of commentary \( c \) to video \( v \) via conditional probability \( P(c|v) \), using retrieval metrics R@1 and MRR to infer epistemic confidence in alignment.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning in GSE maps video moments \( m \) to commentary states \( s_c \) through state transitions \( T(m \to s_c) \), enabling dynamic commentary grounding and event tracking.

reasoning_traces.think:
The primitives form a coherent multimodal grounding framework where video \( v \) and commentary \( c \) are aligned through retrieval \( R \), reordering \( O \), and moment mapping \( M \). These operators define a dual space: one where \( v \) is grounded to \( c \), and another where \( c \) is grounded to \( v \). The retrieval operator \( R(v \to c) \) is modeled as a similarity search in a shared embedding space, with metrics like R@1 and MRR serving as proxies for grounding quality. Frame reordering \( O(f \to c) \) is a permutation optimization problem, solved via learned temporal kernels such as bi-LSTM or bi-GRU. Moment retrieval \( M(c \to v) \) maps semantic commentary to spatiotemporal video segments, relying on attention-based architectures like HERO. Each operator exhibits distinct failure modes: retrieval fails when semantics diverge, reordering fails without temporal cues, and moment retrieval fails with ambiguous commentary. The system is vulnerable to leakage due to preselected highlight clips and lacks full-game grounding.
